payload.excerpt: Follow the Australian seasons month by month, learn what to ask your florist, and see when imported wedding flowers make sense, at home or abroad.
key_takeaways: Set the date before you settle the design, because the month decides which flowers are at their peak, as with waratah, whose flowering is concentrated in spring.
Australian summer is December, January and February, winter is June, July and August, and the northern tropics run on a wet and dry season instead.
Imported cut flowers must meet Australian biosecurity import conditions, so ask your florist which stems are local, which are imported and what the backup is.
For a wedding abroad, the season follows the destination, so the florist there is the one to ask.

faq.q: Which season suits wedding flowers in Australia?
faq.a: No season is wrong for flowers. The better question is which stems are at their peak in your month and region. Set the date first, then ask your florist what will be freshest for it.

faq.q: When should we talk to our florist about substitutes?
faq.a: At the first meeting, once your date and venue are fixed. Agree which flowers are essential and which can be swapped, then review the list as the date approaches and the season's crop becomes clearer.

faq.q: Are imported flowers allowed into Australia?
faq.a: Yes, under conditions. Importers must manage [biosecurity risk](https://www.agriculture.gov.au/biosecurity-trade/policy/risk-analysis/memos/ba2018-12) before cut flowers and foliage are sent to Australia, and some species are subject to [specific conditions of import](https://www.agriculture.gov.au/biosecurity/legislation/fresh-cut-flowers-mainland). Your florist handles this through their suppliers, so your role is simply to ask which stems are imported and what the backup is.

faq.q: What if the flower we love is out of season on our date?
faq.a: Ask your florist for a local alternative in a similar colour and shape, or whether a small number of imported stems could carry it within a mostly local design. Agree in writing what happens if that stem is not available.

faq.q: Which flower is in season in Australian spring?
faq.a: Waratah is a spring flower in Australia, with its flowering [concentrated in that season](https://agrifutures.com.au/related-projects/farm-based-methods-for-control-of-flowering-in-waratahs/). For other stems, ask your florist what is ready locally for your date.

faq.q: Do Australian seasons apply to a wedding overseas?
faq.a: No. The flowers follow the destination's season. In the northern hemisphere, the seasons run in reverse, so ask a florist at the destination what is in season for your date.
